indicators.note: without its heart a word loses its central letter

blocks.note: a response

explanation.surface: A heartless bank sends its reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like the financial institution, but it is the verb, as in to bank on something.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on something is to count on or depend on it, so as verbs the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Maybe anger gripping Head of Circus Smiley?

indicators.note: to grip is to hold, so one piece holds another
the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: anger is one example of a feeling, hence 'maybe'
its first letter

explanation.surface: An angry man takes hold of the head of the Circus, George Smiley.
explanation.walkthrough: In John le Carré's spy novels the Circus is MI6 and George Smiley eventually heads it, so the surface reads as espionage; Smiley is actually the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiley is a typed face like :-) and emoticons are such symbols showing feelings in text.

clue.text: Zeus’s daughter seen within walls of Egyptian city

indicators.note: what lies within walls is the inside, so the outermost letters are dropped

blocks.note: the ancient city of Upper Egypt on the Nile

explanation.surface: A Greek goddess is spotted inside the walls of an ancient Egyptian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the first and last letters, the walls, from THEBES.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe, goddess of youth and cupbearer to the gods, was the child of Zeus and Hera in Greek myth.

clue.text: Prompts Morag finally to feature in candid paintings

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter is used
to feature in something is to appear within it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: paintings of unclothed figures, candid in the sense of revealing all
its last letter

explanation.surface: Morag is finally persuaded to pose for some frank portraits.
explanation.walkthrough: Morag is a Scottish woman's name, chosen only for its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To nudge someone is to give them a gentle push or reminder to act, which is what prompting does.

clue.text: Troubled monk was neglected in confessions

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so these letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: the sixteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A troubled monk feels neglected when hearing confessions.
explanation.walkthrough: The religious picture of monk and confessions is all surface; 'Troubled' works on MONK WAS NEGLECTED.
explanation.definitionFit: An acknowledgement is an admission that something is true, so confessions of fault are admissions of that kind.

clue.text: Indiscipline of kiss stolen by members of the congregation

indicators.note: something stolen is carried off inside the thief's possession, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: lay people, as distinct from clergy
X is the kiss written at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A lapse in standards when churchgoers snatch a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: X goes inside LAITY, the non-clergy members of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Laxity is slackness or lack of strictness, a failure to keep rules firmly enforced.

clue.text: Chemical hailed occasionally by associate of H Jekyll

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: its second, fourth and sixth letters
Edward Hyde, the alter ego of Henry Jekyll in Stevenson's story

explanation.surface: A chemical that Dr Jekyll's companion occasionally greets.
explanation.walkthrough: The initial H for Henry Jekyll points to the matching initial for his other self, Edward Hyde, giving E HYDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldehydes are organic compounds with a CHO group, such as formaldehyde, so the word names a class of chemical.

clue.text: Sculptor starts to explore purchasing stone from Germany

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the first letters are kept

blocks.note: their opening letters
Stein is German for stone

explanation.surface: An artist sets out to buy stone imported from Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone from Germany' looks like the sculptor's raw material, but it means the German word for stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Jacob Epstein was an American-born British sculptor of the twentieth century, known for bronzes and carvings.
